From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cascadeflow.com>, Patrick Dunn <patrick@cascadeflow.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-signature implementation MAP: staged launch, canary, migration & training (CascadeFlow)

Hi Elena / Patrick —

Congrats again on signing — excited to get this into production with you. Attached is the first-draft mutual action plan (MAP_CascadeFlow_v1.2.xlsx) and a concise canary checklist. I pulled together a proposed sequence that balances a fast go-live for your pilot region with risk controls for payment flows. High-level items below; the attached MAP has owner-level rows and dates you can edit.

Proposal (summary):
- Week 0 (Aug 24–28): Provisioning & model pin + test harness; Redwood Dedicated pool reserved. (Owner: Rishi)
- Week 1 (Aug 31–Sep 4): Staged canary A — 1% of live traffic routed to Redwood; telemetry baseline & rollback gates. (Owner: Markus)
- Week 2 (Sep 7–11): Canary B — scale to 10% after QA sign-off; load and latency verification. (Owner: Markus)
- Week 3 (Sep 14–18): Migration window — cutover non-critical flows; data retention config review. (Owner: Monica / CascadeFlow Eng)
- Week 4 (Sep 21–25): Training & enablement — ops playbook, runbook handoff, and two training sessions for on-call and SRE. (Owner: Monica)

Key asks from your side:
1) Confirm procurement contact for PO and any additional contract redlines (DocuSign link provided in related_links).
2) Confirm preferred windows for the two training sessions (we proposed Sep 22 & 24 in the spreadsheet).
3) Identify the single rollback authority during canary windows (we recommend a CascadeFlow engineering lead who can trigger traffic rollback).

I've included a short canary checklist (redwood_canary_checklist.pdf) and a suggested training schedule (training_schedule.csv). If this sequencing looks good, we'll lock dates and circulate the MAP as the canonical source of truth.

Thanks —
Rishi

- Procurement: sending to procurement this morning (procurement@cascadeflow.com) to confirm PO cadence. They asked for a finalized MAP and the master SOW by Friday (Aug 14) so they can attach the PO to the DocuSign envelope.
- Training windows: Sep 22 is good for SRE (US-West), but our ops team prefers Sep 25 (to avoid a payroll close). Can we do one session Sep 22 (SRE) and Sep 25 (Ops)?

Also, small ask — in the MAP please add a short acceptance criteria row for "payment path verification" (we need 5 consecutive days with <0.2% error rate on refunds).

Best,

Elena / team — quick technical notes and a slightly more prescriptive canary runbook (excerpt):

- Canary A (1%):
  - Duration: 48 hours continuous traffic; watch errors, p95 latency, token throughput.
  - Telemetry gates: error rate <0.5% and p95 latency within 1.5x baseline for 2 rolling 1h windows.
  - Rollback criteria: any sustained error rate >0.8% for 30 minutes or a single 5-minute spike >2%.
  - Action: If gate fails, trigger immediate traffic re-route (documented in redwood_canary_checklist.pdf).

- Canary B (10%):
  - Duration: 72 hours; run synthetic storm test for peak hour replicas.
  - Metrics: CPU/GPU utilization <85% sustained and queue depth within configured SLO.

- Migration: we recommend a phased migration per endpoint group (payments first, then refunds, then enrichment). Each group has a 2-hour maintenance window and pre-migration dry-run.

I also added an ops-runbook appendix in the MAP with exact API keys to rotate and a sample curl-based smoke test.

If Patrick is rollback authority, please confirm who on your side we should call (direct line) during the windows so escalation is immediate.

-Markus
Markus Klein | Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
